newsitem.title: GERMANY: Gehe CFO satisfied with oper business.
newsitem.headline: Gehe CFO satisfied with oper business.

text.p: German drugs wholesaler Gehe AG on Tuesday said it was satisfied with its operating business and predicted 1996 sales would be between 20 and 21 billion marks ($13.7 billion), even after its drugs production units are spun off.
"Our operating business is proceeding satisfactorily," Gehe Chief Financial Officer Karl-Gerhard Eick told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He added: "Sales for the year will be between 20 and 21 billion marks." Last year the group posted sales of 19.2 billion marks.
Eick said that the group's share price, which climbed on Monday on the news of the sales but slipped 75 pfennings to 107.00 marks in bourse trade on Tuesday, was satisfactory.
"The share price is OK. It reflects the business accurately," Eick said.
He added however that the share price should rise if Gehe is successful in taking over U.K. group Lloyd's Chemists. Gehe continues to battle U.K. group UniChem Plc for the right to acquire Lloyds.
Eick said Gehe had complied with all requirements set by the U.K. Office of Fair Trade but had not yet received the green light needed to officially submit another bid for the U.K. group.
"We remain interested in Lloyd's Chemists," Eick said declining however to be more specific on whether the group will make a new bid, how high that bid may be and when that bid may be made.
